draft.title: Integrated paragraphs
card: An integrated essay discusses both texts in every body paragraph. Each paragraph is built around one shared idea, such as how both texts treat isolation.
one text is discussed in full, then the other. The reader has to make the links between the texts alone.
both texts appear in each paragraph. The writer puts the texts side by side and does the comparing for the reader.
A strong integrated paragraph opens with a topic sentence about the shared idea, not about one text. It then moves between the texts, with evidence and analysis from each.
draft.remember: Integrated paragraphs put both texts in each paragraph, around one shared idea.

a.q: Which plan for a body paragraph is integrated?
opts: Open with a shared idea, then analyse both texts on it
Analyse the first text fully, then the second text fully
Retell the plot of one text, then explain its themes
Write on one text for three paragraphs, then the other
a.why: An integrated paragraph is built on a shared idea and uses both texts. The block plans keep the texts apart, so the writer does not set them side by side.
a.clue: Look for the plan where both texts share one paragraph.

b.q: Sam is comparing two texts. Which topic sentence best suits an integrated paragraph?
opts: Both texts show that memory shapes a person's sense of home
The first text uses a flashback to show how memory works
The second text is set in a small town in rural Australia
In the first half of the essay, the first text is discussed
b.why: The first option names one idea that both texts share, so the paragraph can use both. The second option names only one text, which leads to block writing.
b.clue: Which sentence gives both texts a place in the paragraph?

a.best: Open with a shared idea, then analyse both texts on it

b.best: Both texts show that memory shapes a person's sense of home

proposal.title: Integrated paragraphs
card: An integrated essay discusses both texts in every body paragraph. Each paragraph is built around one shared idea, such as how both texts treat isolation.
one text is discussed in full, then the other. The reader has to make the links between the texts alone.
both texts appear in each paragraph. The writer puts the texts side by side and does the comparing for the reader.

A strong integrated paragraph opens with a topic sentence about one shared idea: a concern both texts explore, not a plain fact about them. It then moves between the texts, with evidence and analysis from each.
proposal.remember: Integrated paragraphs put both texts in each paragraph, around one shared idea.

a.q: Which essay plan uses an integrated structure?
opts: Each paragraph treats one shared idea across both texts
Three paragraphs on one text, then three on the other
One paragraph per text, then compare them in the conclusion
Each paragraph treats one technique from a single text
a.why: An integrated plan brings both texts into every body paragraph around a shared idea, so the comparing happens throughout. Saving the comparison for the conclusion is still block structure, because the body paragraphs keep the texts apart.
a.clue: In each plan, where does the comparing actually happen?

b.q: Sam is comparing two texts. Which topic sentence best suits an integrated paragraph?
opts: In both texts, memory shapes a person's sense of home
The first text uses flashback to show how memory works
One text explores memory, while the other explores home
Both texts were first published in the same decade
b.why: The sentence about memory shaping a sense of home gives one shared idea that both texts can be analysed on. The sentence that gives memory to one text and home to the other names two separate ideas, so the texts are not compared on the same concern. A shared publication date is a fact, not an idea to analyse.
b.clue: Count the ideas, and check each is a concern rather than a fact.
